To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the laying hen can tolerate a 2 week arrest of egg production without any significant impairment in post-arrest egg production and shell quality, but that the arrest of egg production is associated with a decline in feed intake and body weight.
the induced pause in egg production, in contrast to natural molts, is associated with a rapid increase in egg size and shell thickness.

(1) forced-molt of laying hens results in an increase in the number of eggs per unit of feed consumed, (2) low-Ca treatment results in a decrease in egg production, and (3) Nicarbazin treatment results in an increase of egg production.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects of egg production in laying hens: 1.
the effects of induced pause in egg production on the subsequent performance of the hens.
the effects of induced arrest of egg laying on the subsequent production and shell quality, and on the body weight and feed intake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the laying hens respond to the induced pause of egg production with a significant increase in the rate of production, but not in the proportion of laying hens in the flock.
the effects of a forced pause in egg production depend upon the duration of pause and the method of induction of the pause.
the induced arrest of egg laying, in the present experiments, did not result in a beneficial effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the laying hen is a highly adaptable animal, capable of adjusting to a number of environmental and management factors.

, although the hen can respond to the induced pause in production by an increased egg weight and shell quality and by an increased feed intake, it does not fully restore its pre-arrest production and body weight levels.

, in the laying hen, a pause in egg production is accompanied by a decline of feed intake, and a loss of body-weight, and that the post-arrest performance is significantly influenced by the method of arrest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate of production of laying hens, which is the main determinant of egg output, is highly sensitive to the nutritional and environmental conditions of the birds.
a forced-molting regime, which induces a pause of egg production, can be used to improve production and shell quality of laying hens.
, in a flock of laying hens, a pause of egg production can be induced by a forced-molt or a low-Ca treatment and that the post-arrest production is better than the pre-arrest production.
